title: Operator authorization evidence catalog and stage gates for SSO/RBAC/KMS
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Purpose: Create a single, actionable evidence catalog and staged acceptance gates that product, engineering, and security can use to onboard customers for Private/VPC and on-prem Redwood deployments. Focus areas: SSO (SAML & OIDC), RBAC mapping and delegated roles for operator teams, immutable audit logging (retention & export), and KMS/HSM key custody controls. The deliverable is a checklist + minimum artifacts for each gate, with owners and fallback criteria to unblock customers while maintaining compliance.
scope: In-scope: SSO/SAML configuration templates, RBAC role matrix and delegation flow, audit log schema and retention validation, KMS/HSM key provisioning and proof-of-custody artifacts, runbook for evidence collection. Out-of-scope: changes to Identity Provider (IdP) vendors' features, deep HSM firmware upgrades, or rearchitecting runtime encryption mechanisms.
scope_changes: 2024-11-20: Narrowed evidence set for initial rollout to avoid blocking customers waiting on long HSM lead times — HSM attestation is 'recommended' for GA but 'required' for regulatory customers. 2024-11-28: Added explicit rollback criteria to each gate after incident simulation with ENG team; trade-off accepted: increased operational runbook complexity for faster onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Provided SAML metadata file and verified test assertion exchange with two IdP vendors (Okta, Azure AD) in customer-like environments
RBAC: Role matrix documented and validated by Security; delegated operator role tested to perform non-destructive escalation actions in staging
Audit logs: End-to-end generated audit records for admin actions, immutable export to customer S3-compatible endpoint; retention and checksum verification test pass
KMS/HSM: Key provisioning flow documented; proof-of-custody artifact (signed manifest) exists; customer KMS vendor tested for envelope encryption scenario
Automation: A Confluence-guided checklist generates a PDF evidence bundle; at least one engineer can reproduce onboarding using the checklist within 4 hours
Signoff: Security, Product, and Customer Success provided explicit signoff entries in the checklist for at least two pilot customers
signoff_checklist: Gate 1 (Pre-onboarding): Identity baseline: IdP metadata, SP metadata, test user with SSO access documented
Gate 2 (RBAC mapping): Completed role mapping table and delegated role smoke test results uploaded
Gate 3 (Audit validation): Last 7 days of audit logs exported and CRC checksums validated in customer bucket
Gate 4 (Key handoff): KMS provisioning manifest + key rotation policy and emergency key escrow plan provided
Gate 5 (Operational readiness): Runbooks for incident escalation, key compromise, and audit investigation linked
Gate 6 (Final signoff): Approvals recorded from Security Lead, Product Manager, and Customer Success Manager

decisions: Decision 2024-11-19: Make HSM attestation 'recommended' for general GA; 'required' for regulated customers (legal & security consulted)
Decision 2024-11-27: Use S3-compatible push for audit export rather than syslog pull to reduce customer networking dependencies
Decision 2024-11-30: Require two IdP verifications for onboarding signoff to reduce one-off IdP integration issues

qa_plan: QA will execute a three-customer pilot: internal staging, enterprise pilot with strict HSM requirement, and SMB pilot with soft HSM guidance. Tests: SSO assertion replay, RBAC delegated-role workflows, audit export verification with checksum, and simulated key-rotation emergency. Results documented in Confluence and linked to the evidence bundle.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Pilot): Nov-Dec 2024 - two pilot customers. Phase 2 (Early access): Jan 2025 - allow customers to opt into new checklist. Phase 3 (GA): Feb 2025 - require checklist for all private deployments. Rollback: If audit export or key handoff fails in-prod, automatically pause onboarding for that customer and trigger emergency runbook; fallback to hosted mode until remediation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Long lead time for HSM proofs delays onboarding. Mitigation: Offer a 'soft-attestation' acceptance path for non-regulated customers and clear timeline for HSM compliance. Risk: IdP variability causes integration flakiness. Mitigation: Maintain a set of validated IdP configuration templates and require two successful test assertions before signoff.
next_steps: 1) Finalize Confluence evidence templates (owner: PM). 2) ENG to complete audit export verification and RBAC smoke tests. 3) Security to complete HSM vendor review. 4) Schedule pilot onboarding with two customers and capture evidence bundles. Target: complete pilots by 2024-12-20.
